question.knowledge_point: Integrating Rational Functions With Repeated Factors of Degree Two
question.worked_solution:
First, we convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4x}{(x-2)^{2}} & =\frac{A}{(x-2)}+\frac{B}{(x-2)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,$ and $B,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x-2)^{2}$ and get

$$
4x=A(x-2)+B.
$$

Plugging in $x=2,$ we can eliminate $A$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4(2) & =A(2-2)+B \\ 8 & =0+B \\ B & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Now, plugging in $x=0$ and substituting the known value of $B,$ we can solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4(0) & =A(0-2)+B \\ 0 & =-2A+B \\ 0 & =-2A+8 \\ A & =\frac{8}{2} \\ A & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integrand as the partial sum

$$
\frac{4x}{(x-2)^{2}}=\frac{4}{(x-2)}+\frac{8}{(x-2)^{2}}.
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{3}^{4}\frac{4x}{(x-2)^{2}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{3}^{4}(\frac{4}{(x-2)}+\frac{8}{(x-2)^{2}})\,\text{d}x \\  & =4{\int }_{3}^{4}\frac{1}{x-2}\,\text{d}x+8{\int }_{3}^{4}\frac{1}{(x-2)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-2|{|}_{3}^{4}+8(-\frac{1}{x-2}){|}_{3}^{4} \\  & =4(\operatorname{ln}⁡|4-2|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|3-2|)+8(-\frac{1}{4-2}+\frac{1}{3-2}) \\  & =4(\operatorname{ln}⁡|4-2|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|3-2|)+8(\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡2+4.\end{aligned}
$$
